**Where things stand (as of Oct 14, 2026):** September revenue is already reported. The official figure was released on Oct 8, 2026. I couldn't load the TSMC monthly-revenue page directly, but TSMC's press release and its SEC 6-K filing (an official US securities filing) give the same number. No month has a resolved answer yet.

**Recent official figures**
- **September 2026:** NT$511.86 billion, down 0.6% from August 2026 and up 54.6% from September 2025. This is the number October and November have to beat.
- **August 2026:** NT$514.81 billion, up 10.1% from July. July was NT$467.58 billion. August is the 2026 high so far; CNBC corrected its story to say September was not a record.
- **Third quarter:** about NT$1.49 trillion, beating forecasts and up 50% year on year. The LSEG consensus from 19 analysts was NT$1.46 trillion.
- **Year to date:** January–September revenue was NT$3,898.73 billion, up 41.1%.

**Past years (from my memory, not checked against the official page; NT$ billions)**

| Year | Sep | Oct | Nov | Highest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | ~331.0 | ~367.5 | ~343.6 | October |
| 2024 | ~251.9 | ~314.2 | ~276.1 | October |
| 2023 | ~180.4 | ~243.2 | ~206.0 | October |
| 2022 | ~208.2 | ~210.3 | ~222.7 | November |

- In the last three years, October beat September by roughly 11–35%, usually because a new iPhone and AI product ramps land early in the fourth quarter.
- November usually falls back from October, but it isn't guaranteed: in 2022, November was the highest.
- In 2025, September (~331) was below October and November. By this pattern, September only wins if fourth-quarter revenue drops below the third-quarter level.

**Upcoming events**
- **Third-quarter earnings and fourth-quarter guidance:** scheduled for next week, probably around Oct 15–16. TSMC gives guidance in US dollars only. Dividing the fourth-quarter guidance by 3 and converting at the current exchange rate gives a monthly average to compare with NT$511.86B. Swings in the TWD/USD rate also affect the NT$ figures.
- **October revenue:** expected around Nov 10.
- **November revenue:** expected around Dec 10. The question resolves then.

**What the current data implies:** Nothing is settled. Past patterns favour October, with November second. September wins if both October and November come in below NT$511.86B, and ties go to the earlier month. I didn't look for prediction-market prices.

(a) **Time left:** November revenue is expected around December 10, 2026, about 57 days from today. October’s figure should arrive sooner, around November 10.

(b) **Status quo:** September is the only one of the three months reported so far, at NT$511.86 billion. If October and November do not exceed it, September wins.

(c) **Base rates:** In the four years listed, October was highest three times and November once; September was never highest. October also exceeded September in all four years.

(d) **Unexpected outcome:** A fourth-quarter slowdown or adverse exchange-rate move could leave both later months below September’s already-high figure. Alternatively, a later AI shipment ramp could make November the peak despite October’s usual seasonal advantage.

I favor October’s historical pattern, but September’s strong reported result and the possibility of a November ramp warrant meaningful weight.

(a) **Time left.** About eight weeks. October revenue should be released around November 10, 2026, and November revenue around December 10, 2026. The question resolves at the December release. Q3 earnings and Q4 guidance arrive this week, around October 15–16, and will be informative.

(b) **Status quo.** September is the only month reported so far, at NT$511.86B, so it currently leads by default. It is a fairly high bar. It sits above the Q3 monthly average of about NT$498B and just below August's 2026 high of NT$514.81B.

(c) **Base rates.** These use the research assistant's from-memory figures, which were not checked against the official page.
- October was the highest of Sep/Oct/Nov in 2023, 2024 and 2025. November was highest in 2022. September has not been highest in any of those years.
- In 2023–2025, October beat September by roughly 11–35%.
- Q4 revenue usually exceeds Q3. In 2022 it rose only slightly, about 2%.
- Several factors this year point to Q4 growth in US dollars:
  - persistent AI and CoWoS demand;
  - the N2 ramp for new smartphone chips, which I expect to land in Q4;
  - momentum from Q3 beating consensus.
- If Q4 guidance implies roughly 5–8% quarter-on-quarter growth, the Q4 monthly average would be about NT$520–530B. October, typically the strongest month, would then likely clear NT$512B.

(d) **Unexpected scenarios.**
- **September wins:** TSMC guides Q4 flat or down, for example because of capacity limits or customer inventory timing, or the TWD appreciates sharply against the USD. Both October and November could then print below NT$511.86B. Monthly revenue is lumpy: July came in at only NT$467B within a strong quarter.
- **November wins:** shipment timing pushes revenue into November, as happened in 2022. N2 or CoWoS wafer recognition could plausibly be back-loaded in the quarter.

**Overall:** October is the favourite, November is a meaningful second, and September keeps a non-trivial chance given its high bar and FX risk.
